answer: According to the European Commission against Racism and Intolerance's 2018 work on algorithmic decision-making, AI-driven discrimination can slip past existing anti-discrimination laws because many non-discrimination statutes relate only to specific protected characteristics. There are other forms of discrimination that are not correlated with these protected characteristics but can still reinforce social inequality. This means that AI applications may find ways to "escape current laws," leading to discriminatory outcomes that are not adequately addressed by existing legal frameworks.
